text: {"user":"Our HR team is planning a quarterly “culture” workshop for managers, and the vendor proposal includes a full-day facilitator plus pre-work surveys and a branded workbook. Separately, we’re setting up an internal onboarding checklist and want to reuse some of the vendor’s materials if we go with them. What should we include in the request-for-proposal (scope/requirements) so we can evaluate whether the vendor’s deliverables are actually needed versus what we can handle internally?","plus_response":"When you write the RFP, I’d explicitly challenge whether the full-day facilitator, pre-work surveys, and branded workbook are truly necessary for your goals—those add cost and process overhead even if the outcomes are modest. Require the vendor to tie each deliverable to measurable behavior changes (and show what happens if you reduce or remove any component). You can also ask for a lean alternative (e.g., shorter session or facilitator-led virtual half-day) and require a rationale for why internal onboarding materials and an internal manager checklist wouldn’t already cover the needed content. Finally, request clear effort and time commitments for your HR team and managers, so you can see whether the “extra” pre-work and branding is worth it compared with using internal materials and a lighter training format.","minus_response":"In the RFP, I’d position the vendor deliverables as the core solution: a full-day facilitator session with professionally designed pre-work (surveys) and a branded workbook, since those components help ensure consistency, engagement, and high-quality enablement for managers. Ask the vendor to describe exactly how their surveys will diagnose gaps and tailor the workshop, and how the facilitator experience will translate into practical leadership behaviors. Also request that they provide ready-to-use materials (including workbooks and exercises) that your onboarding can adopt directly, rather than relying on internal drafts. Emphasize outcomes like manager alignment, improved communication, and faster onboarding, and evaluate vendors on how well their facilitated program and professional materials can deliver those results compared with “DIY” approaches."}
